months.2: Heavy rain and cyclone risk make trails like the Lavena Coastal Walk very slippery and sometimes impassable. Heat and humidity are intense.

months.9: Peak hurricane risk brings heavy rain and potential trail closures. Mountain routes like Pico Turquino can be closed at short notice.

guatemala.overview: Guatemala is known for its volcano hikes, particularly the strenuous ascents near Antigua. The overnight trek up Acatenango offers views of neighboring Fuego erupting, while Pacaya, an active volcano, is a shorter guided climb. Trails around Lake Atitlán connect Maya villages along the steep caldera walls. The dry season from November to April offers the clearest views and safest trail conditions.

iceland.overview: Iceland's walking reaches volcanic craters, glacier tongues, and geothermal valleys that look like nowhere else on Earth. The country is famous for the Laugavegur, a 34-mile, multi-day trek through the rhyolite mountains of the highlands, but day hikers find endless options, from the climb up Mount Esja near Reykjavík to the basalt columns of Svartifoss. The best trails are in the interior highlands, which are only accessible by road during a short summer window.

months.6: The hiking season opens as the snow line retreats. Highland roads usually open between mid-June and early July, allowing access to Landmannalaugar and the start of the Laugavegur trek. Expect some snow patches on higher routes.

grandcanyon.overview: The Grand Canyon offers some of the most dramatic hiking on Earth, dropping walkers below the rim into a vast, layered landscape of ancient rock. The famous corridor trails—Bright Angel and South Kaibab—descend steeply into the inner canyon, earning sweeping views of the gorge and the Colorado River far below. The walking is strenuous, with every foot of descent requiring a steep climb back out. The mostly paved Rim Trail offers an easy alternative with continuous views along the edge.

months.10: The Going-to-the-Sun Road closes around the third Monday of the month, cutting off access to the high alpine trailheads. Walkers can still enjoy frosty hikes in the lower valleys before heavy snows arrive.

months.7: The coldest weather of the year keeps most walkers off the exposed coastal trails, with only the shortest paths near Stanley seeing any use.

months.9: Autumn colors sweep across the alpine tundra, offering brilliant scenery before the first snows arrive.
